judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward definitional paragraph assigning labels to identified persons; no term in it carries two plausible meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squares with the rest of the form, though the Lender (DSI) is named here yet given operative rights throughout (e.g., the arbitration section and ENTIRE AGREEMENT clause treat 'you and us' as the only parties), a small latent mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The services are all framed as 'we will attempt to,' with an 'estimated period' of one day and services like 'where available' check cashing and 'maintain a network of branch locations' — vague obligations against which performance for a fee is hard to measure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states the LOC 'secures your repayment of the loan,' which fits the LOC clause, but the fee-for-services framing sits uneasily with COST AND PAYMENT TERMS, which makes the fee an annualized rate on the amount financed rather than a price for the listed services.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, definite: the fee is not interest but is disclosed in the finance charge; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with COST AND PAYMENT TERMS, which likewise includes the CAB fee in the Finance Charge, so no internal tension appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Every material number is a blank ('°%', '$___', 'ofS', 'Joan'), and the promised rebate is described only as 'a prorated daily basis for the final period,' which is not a self-applying formula; the mechanical state of the text materially affects meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The signature block certifies the agreement was delivered 'WITH ALL NECESSARY SPACES COMPLETED,' which the blanks here contradict, and 'earned in advance' sits against the cancellation notice promising return of 'any payment' on cancellation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fees are itemized with figures and a 'whichever is greater' fallback; 'attorneys' fees, and costs of collection' is open-ended but the Collection Expenses clause supplies a reasonableness limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the reimbursement obligation in the LOC clause and the fee recovery in Collection Expenses; the overlap is redundant rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause calls the LOC 'irrevocable' and then provides it is 'automatically revoked' on timely cancellation, and its closing sentences are garbled and truncated ('unlgyuful excess', 'maximug peepee law', 'amortiz'), leaving the compliance savings language incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The truncated savings language reappears whole in the COMPLIANCE clause, so the fragment must be read against it; the revocation-on-cancellation term also has to be harmonised with the three-day Notice of Cancellation forms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'We shall have the right to seek collection of any check or similar security you have provided us' does not say by what means, and the enumerated remedies are followed by the catch-all 'any other right or remedy allowed by law,' a classic general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This right to 'seek collection of any check' runs directly against the Collection Expenses sentence forbidding any person to 'threaten or pursue criminal charges against you related to a check ... provided ... as security for a loan' — the two provisions have to be reconciled to know what collection on a check is permitted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'We may waive or delay enforcing our rights without losing them' and 'we are not required to file suit or arbitrate' are broad, one-sided, and undefined as to scope; 'others responsible' is nowhere defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The anti-waiver and 'not required to ... arbitrate' language must be read against the Arbitration Agreement's election mechanism and the parties' rights to demand arbitration 'even if the other party has begun a lawsuit,' which is exactly where a waiver dispute would be fought.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver is expressed clearly, but the closing condition turns on whether 'you do not reject' the arbitration agreement, a term used nowhere else in the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The arbitration section speaks of 'opting out' within 30 days, not 'rejecting', so the two must be equated by construction; otherwise the jury waiver's carve-out has no operative trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional usury savings clause with a defined self-executing correction; 'amortizing, prorating, allocating and spreading' is standard statutory language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats, in complete form, the truncated savings sentence in the LOC clause and does not conflict with any other term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A reasonable opportunity of not less than 60 days to cure' and 'Any corrective action shall relieve us and Lender of any liability' are both open-ended, and it is unclear whether the notice is a condition precedent to suit only or to arbitration as well.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the Arbitration Agreement, which lets either side elect arbitration of 'any Claim' at any time and preserves a small-claims option, without saying how the 60-day cure period interacts with those routes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence shifts to the third person ('A person may not ... against you ... provided by the consumer'), grafting a statutory prohibition onto a fee clause, and ends with the catch-all 'or other criminal conduct' after forgery, fraud and theft, whose reach is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with the DEFAULT clause's right to 'seek collection of any check or similar security you have provided us' and with the arbitration agreement's promise that all Claims go to arbitration rather than to any court proceeding.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single stipulation of fact with no operative variable; nothing to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the FAA choice in the GOVERNING LAW clause and conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short, definite sentences; 'at our discretion' is one-sided but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere — including the arbitration section's extension of 'we' to affiliates and agents — contradicts the assignment right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely informational addresses and a phone number; no promissory content to interpret.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The notice addresses match those in the pre-suit notice and opt-out provisions, so no inconsistency arises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You and we agree to arbitrate Claims instead of having them decided in court' states an unconditional commitment in a heading sentence whose meaning depends entirely on the qualified provisions that follow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reads as mandatory while 'Starting an Arbitration' makes arbitration arise only 'upon the election' of a party and the definition of Claim expressly preserves small-claims actions and opted-out disputes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Claim' sweeps in 'the actions of you, us, Lender, or third parties' — an almost boundless catch-all sitting beside enumerated categories — and the exclusions ('properly exercised an opt-out right', 'small claims court or equivalent court') are themselves undefined at the edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether conduct such as referring a customer's check to a prosecutor is a 'Claim' must be tested against the DEFAULT and Collection Expenses clauses, and the small-claims carve-out sits against the flat 'agree to arbitrate Claims instead of having them decided in court' opener.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Either you, we, or Lender may give written notice ... at any time, even if the other party has begun a lawsuit' leaves the outer limit of that right open, and arbitrator selection is confined to persons 'reasonably satisfactory to us,' a vague and one-sided standard construed against its drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This unlimited right to demand arbitration must be squared with the NOTICES AND WAIVERS clause ('we are not required to file suit or arbitrate'; delay does not lose rights) and with the pre-suit notice provision, and the judgment cut-off is the only express limit on invoking arbitration after litigating.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The venue options end with 'such other location as we or Lender may agree,' which omits the customer and so does not say whose agreement is needed; the sentence is also mispunctuated mid-clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the rest of the arbitration section and the FAA choice in GOVERNING LAW; no other provision addresses hearing location or fee allocation differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, mechanical entry-of-judgment provision with a deeming rule tied to a determinate fact (home address at the time of the award).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the governing law, venue or severability provisions cuts against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opt-out mechanics are specific (30 days, in writing, named address), but 'Only those disputes ... arising under this Agreement will be excluded' is narrower than the definition of Claim, and the notice address names PLS Financial Services rather than the contracting entity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read with the Claim definition's exclusion for disputes 'in connection with which you properly exercised an opt-out right' and with the jury-waiver clause's reference to 'rejecting' the arbitration agreement; the terminology is not uniform across the three.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain explanatory statement of the consequence of arbitration; it adds no independent obligation to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates the separate WAIVER OF RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY clause without contradiction, although that clause waives jury trial even absent arbitration while this one presupposes arbitration is chosen.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver is stated repeatedly and emphatically with little room for a second reading; the opening conditional ('If either you, we, or Lender ... choose arbitration, all Claims must be arbitrated') is the only loose hinge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the Claim definition and severability clause, though the ban on selecting any organization that permits class arbitration duplicates the selection rules in 'Starting an Arbitration'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard two-sentence severability and conflict-priority rule with definite operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs in mechanism from the ENTIRE AGREEMENT clause, which requires an invalid provision to be 'reformed if practicable', so which regime applies to an invalid arbitration term is not spelled out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite in structure, but saying the arbitration agreement 'is governed by' the FAA leaves open what law supplies its contract-formation and waiver rules.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out has to be harmonised with the Texas-law choice for the rest of the instrument and with the Interstate Commerce stipulation; a dispute over waiver of arbitration would turn on that split.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory-style warning in all capitals with no operative promise; nothing turns on its words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the short-term structure described in the services and cost provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure contact information mandated by regulation; no interpretive content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It does not bear on any other provision, including the pre-suit notice and arbitration terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The entire agreement between you and us relating to the subject matter of this Agreement' is standard, though 'subject matter' is undefined in a transaction that also involves a separate loan with the Lender.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The merger language sits against the separate Credit Services Disclosure Statement and Notices of Cancellation acknowledged in the signature block, and against the Lender's rights created throughout though it is not one of 'you and us'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is a stack of acknowledgments and warranties whose terms are definite, though '(¢)' is a mangled subparagraph label and the bankruptcy warranty ('no intention to file a petition') is a state of mind that cannot be tested.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The certification that the agreement was received 'WITH ALL NECESSARY SPACES COMPLETED' cannot be reconciled with the blank rates, amounts and dates left in COST AND PAYMENT TERMS and in the cancellation notices.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Before midnight of the third day after the date of the transaction' is definite in form, but 'the date of the transaction' is not defined anywhere in the instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The attached Notice of Cancellation measures the same right as 'within three days after the date the contract is signed', a different trigger, so the two cancellation deadlines do not necessarily coincide.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single clear sentence; 'without any penalty or obligation' and 'within three days' are both readily applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its trigger (date the contract is signed) differs from the NOTICE provision's 'date of the transaction', and 'without any penalty or obligation' sits against the CAB fee being 'earned in advance at the inception of the loan'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite refund promise with a fixed 10-day period measured from receipt of notice; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Returning 'any payment made by you under this contract' has to be squared with the CAB fee being earned in advance and with the LOC's automatic revocation on timely cancellation, but the provisions can be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deadline is left blank ('not later than midnight on'), so the operative cut-off date is missing from the form the customer is told to rely on, and the address is stated twice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With the date blank, the deadline must be supplied from the NOTICE clause ('third day after the date of the transaction') or the notice's own 'three days after the date the contract is signed', which are not the same measure.
